home.description: When you first start up your machine it has no idea where the toolhead is positioned, so Marlin needs to use a procedure called “homing” to establish a known position. To do this it moves each axis towards one end of its track until it triggers a switch, commonly called an “endstop.” Marlin knows where the endstops are, so once all the endstops have been triggered the position is known.

jog-y-positive.description: Move the robot by one step in the positive Y direction.

jog-x-negative.description: Move the robot by one step in the negative X direction.

jog-x-positive.description: Move the robot by one step in the positive X direction.

jog-y-negative.description: Move the robot by one step in the negative Y direction.

move-up.description: Move the robot upward along Z by the selected linear step.

move-down.description: Move the robot downward along Z by the selected linear step.

wrist-left.description: Rotate the wrist in the negative direction by the selected wrist step.

wrist-right.description: Rotate the wrist in the positive direction by the selected wrist step.

open-gripper.description: Open the gripper using the configured servo angle.

close-gripper.description: Close the gripper using the configured servo angle.

get-position.description: Get the “current position” of the active tool. Stepper values are included. Normally M114 reports the “projected position” which is the last position Marlin was instructed to move to.

check-endstops.description: Use this command to get the current state of all endstops, useful for setup and troubleshooting. Endstops are reported as either “open” or “TRIGGERED”.

disable-motors.description: Disable the stepper motors on all axes.

stop.description: Stop all steppers instantly. Since there will be no deceleration, expect steppers to be out of position after this command.

restart-after-stop.description: If a STOP occurs you can use M999 to restart the “stopped” machine after resolving the issue.

emergency-stop.description: Used for immediate halt, M112 shuts down the machine, turns off all the steppers, and if possible, turns off the power supply. A reset is required to return to operational mode.
